key_insight: In a real-world cancer registry abstraction test, the strongest LLMs outperformed smaller ones, especially for simpler categorical variables, but struggled more with exact date extraction.
clinical_relevance: LLMs could help speed cancer registry abstraction and reduce manual workload, but they are not yet uniformly reliable across all variable types and cancer types.
method: Evaluated 5 foundational LLMs with zero-shot prompting
Abstracted 8 registry variables from clinical reports
Compared model performance across 5,939 patients with 7 cancer types
evidence_signal: Using hospital registry ground truth, the best models reached about F1 ~0.8 for low-cardinality variables and about 0.55 exact accuracy for diagnosis/treatment dates, improving to about 0.85 with ±30-day tolerance.
watch_item: Performance varied by variable complexity, so exact dates and other high-precision fields may still need human review before operational use.
paper_title: Large language models for cancer registry abstraction: a real-world evaluation across models, variables, and cancer types
